operations_list:
The Operations list contains all the operations in CyberChef arranged into categories. Some operations may be present in multiple categories. You can search for operations using the search box.

To use an operation, either double click it, or drag it into the Recipe pane. You will then be able to configure its arguments (or 'Ingredients' in CyberChef terminology).
search:
Use the search box to find useful operations.

Both operation names and descriptions are queried using a fuzzy matching algorithm.
recipe_pane:
The Recipe pane is where your chosen Operations are configured. If you are a programmer, think of these as functions. If you are not a programmer, these are like steps in a cake recipe. The Input data will be processed based on the Operations in your Recipe.

  • To reorder, simply drag and drop the Operations into the order your require
  • To remove an operation, either double click it, or drag it outside of the Recipe pane

The arguments (or 'Ingredients' in CyberChef terminology) can be configured to change how an Operation processes the data.
hide_args: Clicking 'Hide arguments' will hide all the argument views for every Operation in the Recipe, to save space when you have too many Operation in your Recipe
hide_args_title: Hiding every Operation's argument view in a Recipe
save_recipe:
Recipes can be represented in a few different formats and saved for use at a later date. You can either copy the Recipe configuration and save it somewhere offline for later use, or use your browser's local storage.

  • Deep link: The easiest way to share a CyberChef Recipe is to copy the deep link, either from the address bar (which is updated as the Recipe or Input changes), or from the 'Save recipe' pane. When you visit this link, the Recipe and Input will be populated from where you left off.
  • Chef format: This custom format is designed to be compact and easily readable. It is the format used in CyberChef's URL, so it largely uses characters that do not have to be escaped in URL encoding, making it a little easier to understand what a CyberChef URL contains.
  • Clean JSON: This JSON format uses whitespace and indentation in a way that makes the Recipe easy to read.
  • Compact JSON: This is the most compact way that the Recipe can be represented in JSON.
  • Local storage: Alternatively, you can enter a name into the 'Recipe name' field and save to your browser's local storage. The Recipe will then be available to load from the 'Load Recipe' pane as long as you are using the same browser profile. Be aware that if your browser profile is cleaned, you may lose this data.
load_recipe:
Saved recipes can be loaded using one of the following methods:

  • If you have a CyberChef deep link, simply visit that link and the Recipe and Input will be populated automatically.
  • If you have a Recipe string in any of the accepted formats, paste it into the 'Load recipe' pane textbox and click 'Load'.
  • If you have saved a Recipe to your browser's local storage, it should be available in the dropdown menu in the 'Load recipe' pane. If it is not there, you may not be using the same browser profile, or your profile may have been cleared.
clear_recipe: Clicking the 'Clear recipe' button will remove all operations from the Recipe. It will not clear the Input, but it will trigger a Bake if Auto-bake is turned on, which will change the value of the Output.
step:
The Step button allows you to execute one operation at a time, rather than running the whole Recipe from beginning to end.

Step allows you to inspect the data at each stage of the Recipe and understand what is being passed to the next operation.
bake:
Baking causes CyberChef to run the Recipe against your data. This involves three steps:

  1. The data in the Input is encoded into bytes using the character encoding selected in the Input status bar.
  2. The data is run through each of the operations in the Recipe in turn with the output of one operation being fed into the next operation as its input.
  3. The outcome of the final operation in the Recipe is decoded into Output text using the character encoding selected in the Output status bar.

If there are multiple Inputs, the Bake button causes every Input to be baked simultaneously.
auto_bake:
When Auto-bake is turned on, CyberChef will bake the Input using the Recipe whenever anything in the Input or Recipe changes.

This includes:
  • Adding or removing operations
  • Modifying operation arguments
  • Editing the Input
  • Changing the Input character encoding

If there are multiple inputs, only the currently active tab will be baked when Auto-bake triggers. You can bake all inputs manually using the Bake button.
input_pane:
Input data can be entered by typing it in, pasting it in, dragging it in, or using the 'Load file' or 'Load folder' buttons.

CyberChef does its best to represent data as accurately as possible to ensure you know exactly what you are working with. Non-printable characters are represented using control character pictures, for example a null byte (0x00) is displayed like this: ␀.
tabs:
New tabs can be created to support multiple Inputs. These tabs have their own associated character encodings and EOL separators, as defined in their status bars.

The deep link in the URL bar only contains information about the currently active tab.
open_folder:
You can open a whole folder into CyberChef, which will result in each file being loaded into a separate Input tab.

CyberChef can handle lots of Input files, but be aware that performance may suffer, especially if the files are large in size.

Folders can also be loaded by dragging them over the Input pane and dropping them.
open_file:
Files can be loaded into CyberChef individually or in groups, either using the 'Open file as input' button, or by dragging and dropping them over the Input pane.

CyberChef can handle reasonably large files (at least 500MB, depending on hardware), but performance may be impacted and some Operations will run very slowly over large Inputs.
clear_io: Clicking the 'Clear input and output' button will remove all Inputs and Outputs. It will not clear the Recipe.
reset_layout: CyberChef's panes can be resized to suit your area of focus. This button will reset the pane sizes to their default configuration.
output_pane:
This pane displays the results of the Recipe after it has processed your Input.

CyberChef does its best to represent data as accurately as possible to ensure you know exactly what you are working with. Non-printable characters are represented using control character pictures, for example a null byte (0x00) is displayed like this: ␀.

When copying these characters from the Output, the original byte value will be copied into your clipboard, rather than the control character picture itself.
save_all_outputs:
When operating with multiple tabbed Inputs and Outputs, you can use this button to save off all the Outputs at once in a ZIP file.

Use the 'Bake' button to bake all Inputs at once.

You will be given the choice to specify the file extension for the Outputs, or you can let CyberChef attempt to detect the filetype of each one. If an Output's type is not clear, CyberChef will use the '.dat' extension.
save_all_outputs_title: Saving all outputs to a zip file
save_output: The currently active Output can be saved to a file. You will be asked to specify a filename. CyberChef will attempt to guess the correct file extension based on the data. If a file type cannot be detected, the extension defaults to '.dat' but can be changed manually.
copy_output: Data can be copied from the Output in the normal way by selecting text and copying it. This button provides a quick way of copying the entire output to the clipboard without having to select it. It directly copies the raw data rather than selecting text in the Output editor. Each method will have the same result, but the button may be more efficient for large Outputs as it does not require any DOM interaction.
copy_output_title: Copying raw output to the clipboard
switch_input_output:
This button moves the currently active Output data into the currently active Input tab, overwriting whatever data was already there.

The Input character encoding and EOL sequence will be changed to match the current Output values, so that the data is interpreted correctly.
maximise_output: This button allows you to view the Output pane at maximum size, hiding the Operations, Recipe and Input panes. You can restore the pane to its normal size by clicking the same button again.
breakpoint: Setting a breakpoint on an operation will cause execution of the Recipe to pause when it reaches that operation.
disable_operation: Disabling an operation will prevent it from being executed when the Recipe is baked. Execution will skip over the disabled operation and continue with subsequent operations.
hide_operation_args: Hiding an operation's argument will save space in the Recipe window. Execution will still take place with the selected argument options.
favourite_operations:
This category displays your favourite operations.

  • To add: drag an operation over the Favourites category
  • To reorder: Click on the 'Edit favourites' button and drag operations up and down in the list provided
  • To remove: Click on the 'Edit favourites' button and hit the delete button next to the operation you want to remove
options_settings: Configurable options to change how CyberChef behaves. These settings are stored in your browser's local storage, meaning they will persist between sessions that use the same browser profile.
download_cyberchef:
CyberChef can be downloaded to run locally or hosted within your own network. It has no server-side component so all that is required is that the ZIP file is uncompressed and the files are accessible.

As a user, it is worth noting that unofficial versions of CyberChef could have been modified to introduce Input and/or Recipe exfiltration. We recommend always using the official, open source, up-to-date version of CyberChef hosted at https://gchq.github.io/CyberChef if accessible.

The Network tab in your browser's Developer console (F12) can be used to inspect the network requests made by a website. This can confirm that no data is uploaded when a CyberChef recipe is baked.
multi_type_ingredients: Selecting a data type from the dropdown will change how the ingredient is interpreted by the operation.
population_dropdowns: Selecting a value from this dropdown will populate some of the other ingredients for this operation with pre-canned values.
ingredient_selector: Selecting options in this dropdown will configure which operation ingredients are visible.
status_bar_input: This status bar provides information about data in the Input. Help topics are available for each of the components by activating help when hovering over them.
status_bar_output: This status bar provides information about data in the Output. Help topics are available for each of the components by activating help when hovering over them.
status_bar_input_length:
This number represents the number of characters in the Input.

The CRLF end of line separator is counted as two characters which impacts this value.
status_bar_output_length:
This number represents the number of characters in the Output.

The CRLF end of line separator is counted as two characters which impacts this value.
status_bar_num_lines_input: This number represents the number of lines in the Input. Lines are separated by the End of Line Sequence which can be changed using the EOL selector at the far right of this status bar.
status_bar_num_lines_output: This number represents the number of lines in the Output. Lines are separated by the End of Line Sequence which can be changed using the EOL selector at the far right of this status bar.
status_bar_selection: These numbers show which offsets have been selected and how many characters are in the current selection. If multiple selections are made, these numbers refer to the latest one.
status_bar_cursor_offset_input:
This number indicates what the current offset of the cursor is from the beginning of the Input.

The CRLF end of line separator is counted as two characters which impacts this value.
status_bar_cursor_offset_output:
This number indicates what the current offset of the cursor is from the beginning of the Output.

The CRLF end of line separator is counted as two characters which impacts this value.
status_bar_baking_time:
The baking time is the total time between data being read from the input, processed, and then displayed in the output.

The 'Threading overhead' value accounts for the transfer of data between different processing threads, as well as some garbage collection. It is not included in the overall bake time displayed in the status bar as it is largely influenced by background operating system and browser activity which can fluctuate significantly.
status_bar_input_chr_enc:
The input character encoding defines how the input text is encoded into bytes which are then processed by the Recipe.

The 'Raw bytes' option attempts to treat the input as individual bytes in the range 0-255. If it detects any characters with Unicode values above 255, it will treat the entire input as UTF-8. 'Raw bytes' is usually the best option if you are inputting binary data, such as a file.
status_bar_output_chr_enc:
The output character encoding defines how the output bytes are decoded into text which can be displayed to you.

The 'Raw bytes' option treats the output data as individual bytes in the range 0-255.
status_bar_input_eol:
The End of Line Sequence defines which bytes are considered EOL terminators. Pressing the return key will enter this value into the input and create a new line.

Changing the EOL sequence will not modify any existing data in the input but may change how previously entered line breaks are displayed. Lines added while a different EOL terminator was set may not now result in a new line, but may be displayed as control characters instead.
status_bar_output_eol:
The End of Line Sequence defines which bytes are considered EOL terminators.

Changing this value will not modify the value of the output, but may change how certain bytes are displayed and whether they result in a new line being created.
bombe_loading:
This loading animation shows an accurate representation of how rotors moved on The Bombe, an electro-mechanical device built at Bletchley Park in 1939 by Alan Turing with refinements by Gordon Welchman in 1940. The Bombe was used by the Government Code and Cipher School (the precursor to GCHQ) to discover daily settings of Enigma machines used by the German military in World War 2.

More information can be found on Wikipedia.
stale_indicator: The staleness indicator is displayed when the Recipe or Input has changed but the Output has not yet been updated to reflect this. It is most commonly displayed when Auto-bake is turned off and indicates that you need to Bake in order to see an accurate Output.
magic:
One of CyberChef's best features is its ability to automatically detect which Operations might make more sense of your data. The Magic button appears when CyberChef has a suggested Operation for you based on the data in the Output.

Clicking on the button will add the suggested Operation(s) to your Recipe.

This background Magic detection will inspect your Output up to three levels deep and attempt to unwrap it using a range of techniques. For more control, use the 'Magic' operation, which allows you to configure greater depth and filter based on various parameters.

Further information about CyberChef Magic can be found here.
